facts.text: The study epitaxially deposited a library of ten quinary high-entropy-alloy shells, each containing Fe, Co, Ni, and two platinum-group metals, onto Pd nanocubes.
HER performance was measured in acidic 0.5 M H2SO4, including intrinsic activity at −0.1 V versus RHE and durability over 15,000 cycles.
HOR performance was measured in H2-saturated 0.1 M KOH, including intrinsic activity at 0.1 V versus RHE and durability over 3,000 cycles.
The active PtRuFeCoNi shell was an approximately equiatomic, randomly mixed FCC layer about 1.0 nm thick with a square-arranged {100} surface.
Multielement orbital hybridization and local lattice distortion produced a distribution of adsorption sites that shifted hydrogen binding toward thermoneutral adsorption.
During HER, electron transfer from Fe to Ru increased Ru affinity for hydrogen species, with Ru identified as the direct active site.
DFT gave Pd@PtRuFeCoNi a median hydrogen-adsorption free energy of −0.01 eV, compared with −0.10 eV for Pd@IrRuFeCoNi.
The metastable shell remained randomly mixed through 200°C, developed local L10 order at 300°C and L12 order at 400°C, and phase-separated with a Pt-rich skin at 500°C.
Pd@PtRuFeCoNi showed higher intrinsic HER and HOR activity than commercial Pt/C and the other nine quinary shells.
For HER at −0.1 V versus RHE, Pd@PtRuFeCoNi reached 21.95 mA cm−2 intrinsic activity, 4.5 times the 4.93 mA cm−2 measured for Pt/C.
For HOR at 0.1 V versus RHE, Pd@PtRuFeCoNi reached 0.82 mA cm−2 intrinsic activity, 5.5 times that of Pt/C.
Pd@PtRuFeCoNi lost 7.3% of its HER activity after 15,000 cycles and 16.0% of its HOR activity after 3,000 cycles, versus losses of 22.3% and 55.1%, respectively, for Pt/C.
